page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Uses in alloys
lines: light in mass, so they are used in
steps.why: Magnesium is one of the lightest metals in common use, so its main industrial value is in light alloys, where low mass is what the design needs.
common_mistakes: Writing iron as an alloying metal. Magnesium and iron do not alloy; the ones to name are aluminium, zinc, manganese and tin.
Naming the alloy metals without saying what the alloy is used for.
steps.memory_tip: Aluminium, zinc, manganese, tin: four alloy partners, and the light alloy goes into aircraft.
steps.margin_note: Name the alloying metals and one use of the alloy.

steps.label: Other important uses
lines: with a bright white light, so they
are used in flash powders, flash
in water, called milk of magnesia,
is used as an antacid in medicine.
steps.why: The remaining uses come from two other properties: magnesium burns with an intense white light, and its hydroxide and carbonate are mild bases used in medicine and in toothpaste.
common_mistakes: Writing milk of lime instead of milk of magnesia. Milk of magnesia is Mg(OH)₂ in water, while milk of lime is Ca(OH)₂ in water.
Naming the alloys only. The question asks for the important uses, so the burning and the medical uses belong here too.
steps.memory_tip: Light alloy, bright flame, mild base: three properties and three groups of uses.
steps.margin_note: Milk of magnesia is Mg(OH)₂ in water, not Ca(OH)₂.

insider_note: A list is enough here, but group it by property: the light alloys, the bright flame, and the mild bases used in medicine and toothpaste.
